## Introduction

## Reading in the Data

```{r}
# load packages
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(rsample)

# read in data
# use 'Latin1' for locale 
bike_data <- read_csv("data/SeoulBikeData.csv", locale = locale(encoding = "Latin1"))
```

## Checking the Data (EDA)

```{r}
# check for any missing values (#1)
colSums(is.na(bike_data))

# check structure (#2) ; (can also use 'glimpse' which has a nicer output)
str(bike_data)
glimpse(bike_data)

# convert 'Date' column from chr into actual dates (day/month/year) & confirm change (#3) 
bike_data$Date <- dmy(trimws(bike_data$Date))
glimpse(bike_data)

# take a look at data itself
head(bike_data)

# do summary stats for numeric columns (#2)
summary(bike_data)

# check unique values for categorical variables (#2)
unique(bike_data$Seasons)
unique(bike_data$Holiday)
unique(bike_data$`Functioning Day`)

# turn character variables into factors (Seasons, Holiday, Functioning Day) and check levels (#4)

bike_data$Seasons <- factor(bike_data$Seasons)
levels(bike_data$Seasons)

bike_data$Holiday <- factor(bike_data$Holiday)
levels(bike_data$Holiday)

bike_data$`Functioning Day` <- factor(bike_data$`Functioning Day`)
levels(bike_data$`Functioning Day`)

# double check to make sure structure looks good, specifically for date and factors w/ levels 
str(bike_data)

# rename all variables for easier use & confirm change (#5)
names(bike_data)

bike_data <- bike_data |>
  rename(
    date = Date,
    bike_count = `Rented Bike Count`,
    hour = Hour,
    temp = `Temperature(°C)`,
    humidity = `Humidity(%)`,
    wind_speed = `Wind speed (m/s)`,
    visibility = `Visibility (10m)`,
    dew_point_temp = `Dew point temperature(°C)`,
    solar_radiation = `Solar Radiation (MJ/m2)`,
    rainfall = `Rainfall(mm)`,
    snowfall = `Snowfall (cm)`,
    seasons = Seasons,
    holiday = Holiday,
    functioning_day = `Functioning Day`
  )

names(bike_data)

# create summary statistics for numeric variables (#6)
bike_data |>
  select(
    where(is.numeric)
    ) |>
  summary()

# create summary statistics for categorical variables using bike rental count (#6)  

# by season
bike_data |>
  group_by(seasons) |>
  summarise(
    mean_rentals = mean(bike_count),
    median_rentals = median(bike_count),
    sd_rentals = sd(bike_count),
    total_rentals = sum(bike_count),
    min_rentals = min(bike_count),
    max_rentals = max(bike_count),
    count = n()
  )

# by holiday
bike_data |>
  group_by(holiday) |>
  summarise(
    mean_rentals = mean(bike_count),
    median_rentals = median(bike_count),
    sd_rentals = sd(bike_count),
    total_rentals = sum(bike_count),
    min_rentals = min(bike_count),
    max_rentals = max(bike_count),
    count = n()
  )

# by functioning day
bike_data |>
  group_by(functioning_day) |>
  summarise(
    mean_rentals = mean(bike_count),
    median_rentals = median(bike_count),
    sd_rentals = sd(bike_count),
    total_rentals = sum(bike_count),
    min_rentals = min(bike_count),
    max_rentals = max(bike_count),
    count = n()
  )

# exclude non-functioning observations since rentals won't happen on those days (#6)
bike_data <- bike_data |>
  filter(functioning_day == "Yes")

# summarize across hours so each day has one observation (#7)
daily_bike <- bike_data |>
  # group by date, seasons, and holiday
  group_by(date, seasons, holiday) |>
  
  # find sum of bike_count, rainfall, & snowfall
  summarise(
    bike_count = sum(bike_count),
    rainfall = sum(rainfall),
    snowfall = sum(snowfall),
    
    # find mean of other weather-related variables
    temp = mean(temp),
    humidity = mean(humidity),
    wind_speed = mean(wind_speed),
    visibility = mean(visibility),
    dew_point_temp = mean(dew_point_temp),
    solar_radiation = mean(solar_radiation),
    
    .groups = "drop" # removes grouping
  )

# check new dataset 
glimpse(daily_bike)

# recreate basic summary stats (#8) 

# numeric variables
daily_bike |>
  select(
    where(is.numeric)
    ) |>
  summary()

# categorical variables   

# by season
daily_bike |>
  group_by(seasons) |>
  summarise(
    mean_rentals = mean(bike_count),
    median_rentals = median(bike_count),
    sd_rentals = sd(bike_count),
    total_rentals = sum(bike_count),
    min_rentals = min(bike_count),
    max_rentals = max(bike_count),
    count = n()
  )

# by holiday
daily_bike |>
  group_by(holiday) |>
  summarise(
    mean_rentals = mean(bike_count),
    median_rentals = median(bike_count),
    sd_rentals = sd(bike_count),
    total_rentals = sum(bike_count),
    min_rentals = min(bike_count),
    max_rentals = max(bike_count),
    count = n()
  )

# create plots to explore relationships (#8)

# boxplot: compare daily bike rentals across seasons
ggplot(
  daily_bike, 
  aes(
    x = seasons, 
    y = bike_count
    )) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(
    title = "Daily Bike Rentals by Season",
    x = "Season",
    y = "Number of Daily Bike Rentals"
  ) + 
  theme_grey()

# boxplot: compare daily bike rentals across holidays and non-holidays
ggplot(
  daily_bike, 
  aes(
    x = holiday, 
    y = bike_count
    )) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(
    title = "Daily Bike Rentals by Holiday",
    x = "Holiday (Y/N)",
    y = "Number of Daily Bike Rentals"
  ) +
  theme_grey()

# scatterplot: compare daily bike rentals across temperature 
ggplot(
  daily_bike, 
  aes(
    x = temp, 
    y = bike_count
    )) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(
    method = "lm"
    ) +
  labs(
    title = "Bike Rentals vs. Temperature",
    x = "Temperature (°C)",
    y = "Number of Daily Bike Rentals"
  ) +
  theme_grey()

# report correlation between numeric variables (#8)
daily_bike |>
  select(where(is.numeric)) |>
  cor(use = "complete.obs") |>
  round(2) |>
  as.data.frame() |> # nicer to look at than a matrix, to me personally  
  rownames_to_column(var = "Variable")
```

## Splitting the Data
```{r}
# set seed for reproduction
set.seed(13)

# split data into training and test set (75/25 split) & use 'strata' to stratify the split on 'seasons'
split_bike <- initial_split(
  daily_bike,
  prop = 0.75,
  strata = seasons
)

train_bike <- training(split_bike)
test_bike <- testing(split_bike)

# check number of observations for 75/25 split
nrow(train_bike)
nrow(test_bike)
```

## Fitting a MLR Model

```{r}
# create weekday/weekend variable in training data
train_bike <- train_bike |>
  mutate(
    day_type = factor(
      if_else(
      wday(
        date, 
        week_start = 1
        ) %in% c(6, 7),
      "Weekend",
      "Weekday"
    ), 
    levels = c("Weekday", "Weekend")
    )
  )

# create weekday/weekend variable in testing data
test_bike <- test_bike |>
  mutate(
    day_type = factor(
      if_else(
      wday(
        date, 
        week_start = 1
        ) %in% c(6, 7),
      "Weekend",
      "Weekday"
    ),
    levels = c("Weekday", "Weekend")
    )
  )

# check for new variable
str(train_bike)
str(test_bike)
table(train_bike$day_type)
table(test_bike$day_type)

# create standardized versions of numeric variables 

num_vars <- c(
  "temp", "humidity", "wind_speed", "visibility",
  "dew_point_temp", "solar_radiation", "rainfall", "snowfall"
)

# calculate means using training data
train_means <- sapply(train_bike[num_vars], mean)

# calculate standard deviations using training data
train_sds <- sapply(train_bike[num_vars], sd)

# check
train_means
train_sds

# standardize training data using the training means and sds
train_bike <- train_bike |>
  mutate(
    across(
      all_of(num_vars),
      ~ (.x - train_means[[cur_column()]]) / train_sds[[cur_column()]]
    )
  )

# standardize testing data using the training means and sds
test_bike <- test_bike |>
  mutate(
    across(
      all_of(num_vars),
      ~ (.x - train_means[[cur_column()]]) / train_sds[[cur_column()]]
    )
  )

# fit a model with all the standardized numeric variables included along with the seasons, holiday, and weekend/weekday variables
model1 <- lm(
  bike_count ~ 
    temp + 
    humidity + 
    wind_speed + 
    visibility +
    dew_point_temp + 
    solar_radiation + 
    rainfall + 
    snowfall +
    seasons + 
    holiday + 
    day_type,
  data = train_bike
)

summary(model1)

# fit a model with all the terms in the first model but also interactions between seasons and holiday, seasons and temp, and temp and rainfall

model2 <- lm(
  bike_count ~ 
    temp + 
    humidity + 
    wind_speed + 
    visibility +
    dew_point_temp + 
    solar_radiation + 
    rainfall + 
    snowfall +
    seasons + 
    holiday + 
    day_type +
    seasons:holiday + 
    seasons:temp + 
    temp:rainfall,
  data = train_bike
)

summary(model2)

# fit a model with all the terms in the second model and also squared terms for the temp and humidity variables (standardized versions)
# use I() to create the quadratic terms

model3 <- lm(
  bike_count ~ 
    temp + 
    humidity + 
    wind_speed + 
    visibility +
    dew_point_temp + 
    solar_radiation + 
    rainfall + 
    snowfall +
    seasons + 
    holiday + 
    day_type +
    seasons:holiday + 
    seasons:temp + 
    temp:rainfall +
    I(temp^2) + 
    I(humidity^2),
  data = train_bike
)

summary(model3)

# predict daily bike rentals for each model using test data
pred1 <- predict(model1, newdata = test_bike)
pred2 <- predict(model2, newdata = test_bike)
pred3 <- predict(model3, newdata = test_bike)

# find test set RMSE for each model 
rmse1 <- sqrt(mean((test_bike$bike_count - pred1)^2))
rmse2 <- sqrt(mean((test_bike$bike_count - pred2)^2))
rmse3 <- sqrt(mean((test_bike$bike_count - pred3)^2))

# compare RMSE values
rmse_results <- tibble(
  Model = c("Model 1", "Model 2", "Model 3"),
  RMSE = c(rmse1, rmse2, rmse3)
)

# display results (from lowest to highest RMSE) & determine which model minimizes this test set RMSE
rmse_results |>
  arrange(RMSE)
# model 3 has the lowest RMSE

# create weekday/weekend variable for the entire data set
full_bike <- daily_bike |>
  mutate(
    day_type = factor(
      if_else(
        wday(
          date, 
          week_start = 1
          ) %in% c(6, 7),
        "Weekend",
        "Weekday"
      ),
      levels = c("Weekday", "Weekend")
    )
  )

# check for new variable
str(full_bike)
table(full_bike$day_type)

# calculate means and sds using the full dataset
full_means <- sapply(full_bike[num_vars], mean)
full_sds <- sapply(full_bike[num_vars], sd)

# check 
full_means
full_sds

# standardize numeric predictors using the full dataset
full_bike <- full_bike |>
  mutate(
    across(
      all_of(num_vars),
      ~ (.x - full_means[[cur_column()]]) / full_sds[[cur_column()]]
    )
  )

# fit model 3 using full dataset 
final_model <- lm(
  bike_count ~ 
    temp + 
    humidity + 
    wind_speed + 
    visibility +
    dew_point_temp + 
    solar_radiation + 
    rainfall + 
    snowfall +
    seasons + 
    holiday + 
    day_type +
    seasons:holiday + 
    seasons:temp + 
    temp:rainfall +
    I(temp^2) + 
    I(humidity^2),
  data = train_bike
)
```
